terms.gloss: slip, lose one’s footing; slip down
evidence: Hor. S. 2.1.15; Cic. Fat. 5 (Lewis & Short: “of sinking, slipping down”)
terms.comment: To slide and begin to fall, as when a foot goes from under one (Lewis & Short: “to sink as the beginning of a fall”). Moving smoothly through the air or over ice is the same verb in another sense (see glide).

phrases.latin: Cavē nē lābāris: pavīmentum lūbricum est.
phrases.english: Mind you don’t slip: the floor is slippery.
He slipped on the ice and fell.

sources: Lewis & Short: labor
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 381.
